title: Exception fidelity — `Err(ExecError)` where BEAM demands a catchable raise (try_case_end, body-position bif/gc_bif, >60-bit binary integer match) + the systematic sibling sweep
purpose:
Ground: `docs/REVIEW-23-07.md` (reviewed at `fd71c5e`, 2026-07-23; 11 parallel subsystem reviewers, each finding adversarially re-verified by an independent refuter). Its recommended priority order names this cluster at rank 3: "H1, H2, M1 — exception fidelity: the 'returns `Err(ExecError)` where it should `raise_exception`' bug-class is uncatchable-and-mislabeled; sweep for remaining siblings." This brief is that item. Evidence pin for THIS brief: beamr main `a0359a2`. Re-pin note: none of the three cited files moved for the cited lines between `fd71c5e` and `a0359a2` (`exceptions.rs` and `guards.rs` are byte-identical across that range; `matching.rs` changed only at `allocate_binary` (`:625-636`, the AllocKind refcount fix), which is below all cited sites) — the review's line numbers hold verbatim at the current head.

THE DEFECT CLASS, stated once. `run_loop` (`crates/beamr/src/interpreter/mod.rs:265-312`) dispatches every instruction through `opcodes::dispatch_with_services(...)?` — the `?` is the whole story. An `Err(ExecError)` returned by an opcode handler propagates OUT of `run_loop` without ever consulting `process.pop_exception_handler()`, so it CANNOT be caught by the running process's own `try`/`catch`, and its ExecError variant is a Rust-side classification that discards whatever class/reason BEAM specifies. The correct seam already exists in the same module tree: `exceptions::raise_exception` (`crates/beamr/src/interpreter/opcodes/exceptions.rs:176-201`) pops the handler, truncates the stack, prunes native continuations, writes the destination (Try) or the caught tuple (Catch), and returns `InstructionOutcome::Jump(handler.catch_position)` — or, with no handler, `InstructionOutcome::Exit(ExitReason::Error)` carrying the true class/reason. Every opcode that models a BEAM-defined exception MUST go through that seam.

PRECEDENT — this is the third and fourth pass over the same class, and both prior passes are in `git log` at this head:
  * `5bcd529` `fix(interpreter): func_info raises catchable function_clause instead of looping` — `ExecError::FunctionClause` was NEVER CONSTRUCTED anywhere in `src`; a no-matching-clause function LOOPED FOREVER. Fixed to raise bare-atom `error:function_clause` through `raise_exception`, "the same seam as `case_end`/`if_end`. No new exception machinery." Fail-first was loaded-bytecode catchability on a real-erlc `fc_probe` fixture (`crates/beamr/tests/function_clause_e2e.rs`, `tests/fixtures/fc_probe.{erl,beam}`), watchdog-bounded, RED before / GREEN after.
  * `0a1f6ed` `fix(interpreter): if_end raises bare-atom if_clause, not {if_clause,[]}` — the reason SHAPE was wrong, so `catch error:if_clause` failed to match and the process died where BEAM recovers. Crucially it also records the RE-PIN doctrine: the unit test `case_if_and_try_case_end_build_catchable_error_reasons` (`exceptions.rs:689`) had PINNED the wrong `{if_clause,[]}` tuple — "a self-consistent-but-wrong pin (measured against the artifact it gates, not against BEAM)". Same pattern applies here: that test's `try_case_end` half is currently absent and its badmatch assumption must not be allowed to re-pin the wrong reason.
H1/H2/M1 are the LIVE SIBLINGS the review names explicitly ("This is the exact bug-class the recent `func_info`/`if_end` fixes addressed — these are live siblings").

THE THREE PINNED DEFECTS at `a0359a2`:
  * H1 — `crates/beamr/src/interpreter/opcodes/exceptions.rs:81` (review `fd71c5e:81`, UNMOVED). `try_case_end` builds `two_tuple(process, Term::atom(Atom::BADMATCH), value)`. BEAM raises `error:{try_clause, V}` when a `try Expr of Pat -> ... catch ... end` success value matches no `of` clause. The reason is not merely mislabeled: `try_clause` IS NOT IN THE ATOM TABLE — `crates/beamr/src/atom/table.rs:14-90` runs `OK(0) .. INFINITY(76)` with no `TRY_CLAUSE`, and `COMMON_ATOMS` (`:101-179`) has no `("try_clause", ...)` row. So `error:{try_clause,_}` handlers in loaded bytecode miss and `error:{badmatch,_}` handlers WRONGLY FIRE — a silent mis-branch, not a crash. The instruction is fully wired and reachable: decode `loader/decode/code.rs:297` (opcode 107) -> `Instruction::TryCaseEnd` (`loader/decode/instruction.rs:214`) -> dispatch `interpreter/opcodes/mod.rs:382`.
  * H2 — `crates/beamr/src/interpreter/opcodes/guards.rs:255-256` (review cited `:255`, UNMOVED; the `return Err(ExecError::Badarg)` is at `:256` inside the `if label == 0` at `:255`). In `guards::bif` (`:177`, serving BOTH `bif` and `gc_bif` via `opcodes/mod.rs:348`), the native call result is matched as `Err(_) => { context.detach_process(); let label = core::operand_label(parsed.fail)?; if label == 0 { return Err(ExecError::Badarg); } jump_label(module, parsed.fail) }`. THE `Err(_)` DISCARDS THE REASON TERM. Body position is exactly fail-label 0, so `1 div 0` — `div` is a registered Pure BIF (`native/bifs.rs:27`, impl `:101`) that returns `Err(Term::atom(Atom::BADARITH))` (`native/bifs.rs:427`) — surfaces as an UNCATCHABLE `ExecError::Badarg` instead of a catchable `error:badarith`. Both the catchability and the label are wrong, from one `Err(_)`.
  * M1 — `crates/beamr/src/interpreter/opcodes/binary/matching.rs:83` (review `fd71c5e:83`, UNMOVED) in `bs_get_integer`: `let term = Term::try_small_int(value).ok_or(ExecError::Badarg)?;`. `Term::SMALL_INT_MAX`/`MIN` (`term/mod.rs:36-37, 90-93, 118-125`) bound the immediate int at PAYLOAD_BITS, so `<<X:64>>` with a value at or beyond 2^60 returns `None` and raises an uncatchable, mislabeled `badarg` — although the boxed bignum representation EXISTS and is used elsewhere (`term/boxed/mod.rs:157-168` `write_bigint`, `BoxedTag::BigInt = 0x12`; live callers at `native/context/alloc.rs:208`, `mailbox/mod.rs:415`, `term/json.rs:291-330`). LIVE SIBLING FOUND DURING RE-PIN, NOT IN THE REVIEW: the identical construction appears a second time at `matching.rs:468` in the `bs_match` `("integer", [_live, flags, size, unit, dst])` command arm — the OTP-27+ `bs_match` lowering path. Both are in scope. Two upstream refusals in `get_integer_value` (`matching.rs:553-555` `if size_bits > 63 { return Err(ExecError::Badarg) }`; `decode_integer` `matching.rs:874-877` `if bytes.len() > size_of::<i64>() { return Err(ExecError::Badarg) }`) cap the DECODE at 64 bits and are part of the same defect surface.

WHY THIS CLASS IS WORTH A SWEEP AND NOT THREE PATCHES: `Err(ExecError::Badarg)` is the single most common refusal shape in the interpreter — 135 `ExecError::Badarg` mentions across `crates/beamr/src/interpreter` at this head (vs 119 `InvalidOperand`, 13 `Badfun`, 12 `Undef`, 5 `Badarity`, 5 `Badarith`), 137 `Err(ExecError::` returns total. Some of those are genuinely-uncatchable-by-design (malformed bytecode the loader/validator should already have rejected); some are H2-shaped live defects. Nobody can tell which by eye, and four separate passes over this class (func_info, if_end, and now H1/H2/M1) have each found more. The sweep with an auditable artifact is the point of the brief, not a nicety.
task:
DESIGN STANCE (decided): every opcode that models a BEAM-DEFINED exception raises through `exceptions::raise_exception` with the class and reason BEAM specifies; every remaining `Err(ExecError::...)` on an interpreted-code-reachable path is either converted or WRITTEN DOWN as genuinely-uncatchable-by-design with its reason. No new exception machinery, no new wake paths, no timers, no configuration. OTP-29 is the reference semantics for every fidelity claim in this brief and every differential must be run against it by hand, as `5bcd529`/`0a1f6ed` did.

D1 RED FIRST, LOADED BYTECODE (R1). The catchability proof is loaded bytecode and nothing else — `0a1f6ed`'s standard, verbatim: "a Rust-side variant is not evidence". Three real-erlc `.erl` + `.beam` fixture pairs committed under `crates/beamr/tests/fixtures/` (house convention; `erlc` is on the box at `/opt/homebrew/bin/erlc`; beamr-authored sources, never another project's artifact bytes), each driven through the real threaded scheduler with a watchdog deadline (the `fc_probe`/`if_probe` harness shape — `crates/beamr/tests/if_clause_e2e.rs:14-46` is the template: `BifRegistryImpl::new()`, `load_module(include_bytes!(...))`, single-thread `SchedulerConfig`, `DEADLINE = 5s`). Arguments routed through an `id/1` to defeat constant folding, exactly as `if_probe` does.

D2 H1 FIX. `try_case_end` raises `error:{try_clause, V}`. Requires a NEW `Atom::TRY_CLAUSE` — minting is mechanical and index-order-sensitive: append `pub const TRY_CLAUSE: Self = Self(77);` after `INFINITY: Self = Self(76)` (`atom/table.rs:90`) AND the matching `("try_clause", Atom::TRY_CLAUSE)` row at the END of `COMMON_ATOMS` (`:178`). The two must stay index-aligned: `with_common_atoms` (`:205-217`) inserts by `atom.index()` and then stores `next_index = COMMON_ATOMS.len()`, so a const whose index is not its row position corrupts every subsequent `intern`. Reason SHAPE is the 2-tuple `{try_clause, V}` carrying the offending value (like `badmatch`/`case_clause`, NOT like the bare-atom `if_clause`/`function_clause`) — confirm on OTP-29 before landing, per the `0a1f6ed` shape lesson.

D3 H2 FIX — the load-bearing one. In `guards::bif` (`guards.rs:245-260`) replace `Err(_)` with `Err(reason)` and mirror `native_call.rs:216-223` EXACTLY: take the class and stacktrace off the context BEFORE detaching (`context.take_exception_class()` / `context.take_exception_stacktrace()`, `native/context/mod.rs:1522-1530, 1684-1688`), `context.detach_process()`, then for fail-label 0 build `crate::process::Exception { class: Term::atom(core::exception_class_atom(class)), reason, stacktrace }` and `return super::exceptions::raise_exception(process, exception)`. `exception_class_atom` is already `pub(super)` in `opcodes/core.rs:56` and already imported by `native_call.rs:21`. THE GUARD-POSITION PATH IS UNTOUCHED: fail-label != 0 still `jump_label(module, parsed.fail)` — a failing guard BIF branches, it does not raise; that is the BEAM contract and the behavioral twin R5 pins it. Ordering constraint: `raise_exception` needs `&mut Process`, which `context.attach_process` holds — detach first, as `native_call.rs` does.

D4 M1 FIX. Both `Term::try_small_int(value).ok_or(ExecError::Badarg)?` sites (`matching.rs:83` in `bs_get_integer`, `matching.rs:468` in the `bs_match` `integer` command) bind a bignum when the decoded value does not fit an immediate. Two hard constraints the drafter must respect: (a) GC — a bignum is a HEAP allocation; `bs_get_integer` currently reserves NO space before its write (contrast `bs_get_float` at `:91`, which calls `gc::ensure_space(process, 2, 256)` BEFORE `read_context`), and the `MatchContext` is a heap pointer, so the reserve must happen BEFORE `read_context` or the context must be re-read after — this is the H3/H5 stale-Term-across-`ensure_space` class the same review names, and introducing an instance of it here is a STOP; (b) the `bs_match` arm at `:468` runs inside a command loop whose space was reserved BEFORE the loop began (see the `float` arm comment at `:477`), so the per-command bignum worst case must be folded into that pre-loop reservation, not reserved mid-loop. Residual refusals that remain genuinely impossible-to-satisfy raise catchable `error:badarg` via `raise_exception`, never bare `Err`. The decode-side 64-bit caps (`get_integer_value` `:553-555`, `decode_integer` `:874-877`) are IN SCOPE for classification: either widened to produce a multi-limb value, or documented in the R6 artifact with the BEAM behavior they diverge from and a tracking line — the drafter states which, with reasons.

D5 THE SWEEP (R6) — a requirement with an artifact, not a vibe. Enumerate EVERY `return Err(ExecError::...)` / `.ok_or(ExecError::...)` / `.ok_or_else(|| ExecError::...)` / `?`-on-`ExecError` construction site in `crates/beamr/src/interpreter/**` reachable from interpreted code (universe at this head: 137 `Err(ExecError::` returns; the `Badarg`/`Badarith`/`Badfun`/`Badarity`/`Undef` variants — the ones that NAME a BEAM reason — are the primary suspects at 170 mentions; `InvalidOperand` at 119 is the presumptive malformed-bytecode class but presumption is not proof and each site still gets a row). Every site gets exactly one classification with a stated reason:
  (a) CONVERTED — BEAM defines a catchable exception here; fixed in this lane, red-first, with the OTP-29 differential recorded.
  (b) UNCATCHABLE BY DESIGN — malformed bytecode / broken loader invariant / VM-composition failure that no Erlang program can provoke and no `try` should absorb. Requires the ARGUMENT, not the assertion: what prevents interpreted code from reaching it (loader validation? `loader/validate.rs` line? decoder shape? type invariant?).
  (c) DEFERRED — real defect, out of this lane's scope; row carries the reason and where it is tracked.
Artifact: a committed markdown table `docs/design/beamr/briefs/evidence/RF-004-exec-error-sweep.md` — columns `file:line | variant | opcode/function | reachable from interpreted code? | BEAM behavior | classification | disposition` — AND the same census summarized in the landing commit message. A row per site; no `... and 40 others`. The sweep is the deliverable that makes the fifth pass over this class unnecessary.

D6 SCOPE FENCE. C1/C2 (the two critical memory-safety bugs), H3/H4/H5 (the GC-move-across-unrooted-Term class), H6/M7/M9 (untrusted-input DoS) are OTHER LANES from the same review and are NOT touched here. M2/M3/M6 are RF-007. M12 is RF-005. If the sweep surfaces a site whose correct fix is a memory-safety change, it is classified (c) DEFERRED with a pointer — never fixed opportunistically inside this lane.

OQ-1 (drafter's call, stated in the handoff): whether the M1 decode-side widening (D4, `get_integer_value` `:553-555` / `decode_integer` `:874-877`) lands in this lane or is classified (c) with a tracking row. Bias: bind-the-bignum for the values the decoder ALREADY produces is in scope; widening the decoder to multi-limb magnitudes beyond 64 bits is a separate build if it costs more than a contained change.

requirements.title: RED — loaded-bytecode catchability fixtures for H1, H2, M1 (all three failing at `a0359a2`)
requirements.spec: Per D1: three beamr-authored real-erlc `.erl` + `.beam` fixture pairs plus their integration tests, committed and demonstrably RED at current bytes BEFORE any fix lands. (i) H1 — `try id(ok) of other -> fine catch error:{try_clause, _} -> caught end`: OTP-29 returns `caught`; beamr currently raises `{badmatch, ok}`, the `try_clause` clause misses, the process dies Error. A twin assertion pins the WRONG-FIRING half: a `catch error:{badmatch,_}` handler currently catches and must stop catching. (ii) H2 — `try id(1) div id(0) catch error:badarith -> caught end` in BODY position (fail label 0): OTP-29 returns `caught`; beamr currently propagates `ExecError::Badarg` out of `run_loop`, bypassing the handler entirely. (iii) M1 — `<<X:64>> = <<Big:64>>` binding a value at/above 2^60 then returning it: OTP-29 binds the bignum; beamr currently raises uncatchable badarg. Watchdog-bounded (`DEADLINE = 5s`, `fc_probe`/`if_probe` harness shape), arguments routed through `id/1` to defeat constant folding.
acceptance: All three fixture tests exist, compile, and FAIL at `a0359a2` with the exact wrong behavior transcribed into the test's failure message (H1: reason tuple head is `badmatch`; H2: process exit is Error with the handler never entered; M1: uncatchable badarg) — the RED transcript is recorded in the commit body
Each `.erl` is beamr-authored and compiled by the box's real OTP-29 `erlc`; both `.erl` and `.beam` are committed; NO other project's artifact bytes are used
The OTP-29 differential for all three is run by hand and its verbatim output recorded in the commit body — the reference-semantics claim is measured, not asserted
H2's guard-position twin (fail-label != 0) is asserted GREEN in the same RED commit: a failing guard BIF branches to its fail label and does NOT raise, before and after the fix

requirements.title: H1 — `try_case_end` raises `error:{try_clause, V}`; `try_clause` is minted in the atom table
requirements.spec: Per D2: `Atom::TRY_CLAUSE = Self(77)` appended after `INFINITY` in `atom/table.rs`, with its `("try_clause", Atom::TRY_CLAUSE)` row appended at the END of `COMMON_ATOMS` at the SAME position index; `exceptions::try_case_end` (`exceptions.rs:74-83`) builds `two_tuple(process, Term::atom(Atom::TRY_CLAUSE), value)`. The reason SHAPE (2-tuple carrying the offending value) is confirmed against OTP-29 before landing.
acceptance: R1(i) goes GREEN: `catch error:{try_clause, ok}` catches in loaded bytecode; the twin `catch error:{badmatch,_}` no longer catches

Atom index and COMMON_ATOMS row position are aligned — a test asserts `with_common_atoms().resolve(Atom::TRY_CLAUSE) == Some("try_clause")` AND that `with_common_atoms().len()` equals `COMMON_ATOMS.len()`, so a future misaligned mint is caught at the table, not at a mis-resolved error string
`Atom::BADMATCH` is no longer constructed by `try_case_end` (grep); `exceptions::badmatch` (`:143-152`) is UNCHANGED — the real badmatch opcode keeps its reason

The `case_if_and_try_case_end_build_catchable_error_reasons` unit test (`exceptions.rs:689`) is EXTENDED with a `try_case_end` leg asserting `{try_clause, V}`; per the `0a1f6ed` re-pin lesson the assertion is measured against OTP-29, not against beamr's prior output

requirements.title: H2 — body-position `bif`/`gc_bif` failure raises the native's true class and reason through `raise_exception`
requirements.spec: Per D3: `guards::bif` (`guards.rs:245-260`) binds `Err(reason)`, takes `context.take_exception_class()` and `context.take_exception_stacktrace()` BEFORE `context.detach_process()`, and for fail-label 0 raises `crate::process::Exception { class: Term::atom(core::exception_class_atom(class)), reason, stacktrace }` via `super::exceptions::raise_exception(process, exception)` — the `native_call.rs:216-223` pattern verbatim. Fail-label != 0 keeps `jump_label(module, parsed.fail)` byte-identical.
acceptance: R1(ii) goes GREEN: `1 div 0` in body position is catchable as `error:badarith` in loaded bytecode, matching the recorded OTP-29 differential; the reason Term is the native's own (`Atom::BADARITH` from `native/bifs.rs:427`), not a re-classification
A `throw`-class native (one that calls `context.set_exception_class`) reaching body position surfaces with its class preserved — the class channel is proven live, not just the reason channel
`ExecError::Badarg` is no longer constructed anywhere in `guards::bif`'s native-call result handling (grep on the function body)
GUARD POSITION UNCHANGED: the fail-label != 0 branch is byte-preserved and its behavioral twin (R1's guard-position assertion) is green before and after — a failing guard BIF branches, never raises
The context is detached before `raise_exception` is called; no borrow of `process` is held across the raise

requirements.title: M1 — binary integer matching binds a bignum instead of raising uncatchable badarg, at BOTH construction sites, without introducing a stale-Term-across-`ensure_space`
requirements.spec: Per D4: `matching.rs:83` (`bs_get_integer`) and `matching.rs:468` (the `bs_match` `integer` command) bind a boxed bignum via `term::boxed::write_bigint` when the decoded value exceeds `Term::SMALL_INT_MAX`/`MIN`. Heap space is reserved BEFORE the `MatchContext` is read (or the context is re-read after the reserve) at `:83`; at `:468` the bignum worst case is folded into the pre-loop reservation `bs_match` already performs. Any residual unsatisfiable case raises catchable `error:badarg` through `raise_exception`, never a bare `Err`.
acceptance: R1(iii) goes GREEN: a >60-bit binary integer match binds a bignum whose value round-trips exactly, matching the recorded OTP-29 differential, at BOTH the `bs_get_integer` and `bs_match` lowerings (the second site was found during re-pin and is NOT in the review — a fixture clause exercises each lowering explicitly)

GC SAFETY, explicitly proven: no `MatchContext` or heap-interior `Term`/slice is held across the new allocation or across any `ensure_space` — the re-read-after-reserve pattern `bs_get_float` (`matching.rs:91-99`) and the rest of the file already use. A reviewer-checkable note names the reserve point and the re-read point for each site. Introducing an H3/H5-class instance here is a STOP

Signed and unsigned, big- and little-endian 64-bit segments all bind correct values across the small-int boundary (at, one below, one above `SMALL_INT_MAX`, and the negative mirror) — boundary coverage, not a single sample

The decode-side 64-bit caps (`get_integer_value:553-555`, `decode_integer:874-877`) are resolved per OQ-1: either widened with tests, or classified (c) in the R6 artifact with the BEAM divergence written down. The handoff states which and why

requirements.title: Permanent walls — the raise seam cannot silently regress
requirements.spec: The three e2e fixtures from R1 become permanent release-gated walls, plus a lib-side wall per fix asserting the exact reason/class payload at the seam (not just the observable outcome): `try_case_end` yields `{try_clause, V}`; `guards::bif` at fail-label 0 yields the native's reason with the native's class and CONSULTS the handler; the bignum bind produces a `BoxedTag::BigInt` term of the exact value.
acceptance: All three e2e tests run under `cargo test --workspace` (the gates.json `tests` leg) and pass ten consecutive isolated runs each

Fail-first recorded and reverted, per fix independently: revert R2 -> the H1 wall goes red at the reason-head assert; revert R3 -> the H2 wall goes red with the process dying uncaught; revert R4 -> the M1 wall goes red at the uncatchable badarg. Each RED transcript is in the landing commit body
The lib-side payload walls assert the CLASS as well as the reason for R3 — a fix that raises the right reason under the wrong class must go red

requirements.title: THE SWEEP — every remaining interpreter `Err(ExecError::...)` classified, with a committed auditable artifact
requirements.spec: Per D5: enumerate every `ExecError` construction site in `crates/beamr/src/interpreter/**` reachable from interpreted code and classify each as (a) CONVERTED, (b) UNCATCHABLE BY DESIGN with the argument for why interpreted code cannot reach it, or (c) DEFERRED with a reason and a tracking pointer. Artifact: `docs/design/beamr/briefs/evidence/RF-004-exec-error-sweep.md`, a table with columns `file:line | variant | opcode/function | reachable from interpreted code? | BEAM behavior | classification | disposition`, plus the census summary in the landing commit message.
acceptance: The census is COMPLETE and mechanically reproducible: the artifact states the exact grep(s) that generate the universe and the count they returned at the build base, and the table row count equals that universe (at `a0359a2` the universe is 137 `Err(ExecError::` returns across `crates/beamr/src/interpreter`; the build base may differ and the artifact records its own number)

EVERY row carries a classification and a REASON. Zero rows read `unclear`, `probably fine`, or elide siblings with `...`. A (b) row that merely asserts unreachability without naming the mechanism (loader validation site, decoder shape, type invariant) is not acceptable

Every (a) row found by the sweep beyond H1/H2/M1 is fixed IN THIS LANE red-first with its own fixture and its own OTP-29 differential, or is downgraded to (c) with the reason stated — the drafter does not get to silently drop a found defect
Every (c) row names where it is tracked; C1/C2/H3/H4/H5/H6/M7/M9 rows point at their own lanes and are NOT fixed here (D6 scope fence)
A grep-based prohibition wall lands with the artifact: the specific sites classified (a)-and-fixed cannot reacquire a bare `Err(ExecError::Badarg)` without turning a test red

boundaries: GUARD-POSITION SEMANTICS UNCHANGED: a guard BIF failing with fail-label != 0 branches to that label. Only body position (fail label 0) changes from `Err` to a raise. Anything that changes WHEN or WHETHER a guard branches is a STOP.

No new exception machinery. `raise_exception` (`exceptions.rs:176-201`) is the seam; the handler stack, stacktrace capture, and native-continuation pruning are untouched — the `5bcd529` standard, verbatim.

OTP-29 IS THE REFERENCE. Every fidelity claim (reason atom, reason SHAPE bare-vs-tuple, class) is measured against OTP-29 by hand and the output recorded, never inferred from beamr's own prior behavior. `0a1f6ed`'s self-consistent-but-wrong pin is the standing lesson: an existing beamr test asserting the current shape is EVIDENCE OF NOTHING.

Loaded bytecode is the catchability proof. A Rust-side unit test that calls the opcode handler directly is a payload wall, not a catchability wall; both are required and neither substitutes for the other.

NO STALE TERM ACROSS A GC-CAPABLE ALLOCATION. R4 adds heap allocation to the binary-match path; the H3/H4/H5 defect class from the same review must not gain a new instance. Reserve before reading the match context, or re-read after — and say which, in the code, at the site.

ZERO new `#[allow]` of any kind; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`; no `_ =>` catch-all arms introduced to dodge an exhaustive match — the new `Atom::TRY_CLAUSE` and any widened match must be handled honestly, and the sweep must be honest about what it did not classify.
`crates/beamr/src/loader/encode/**` is UNTOUCHABLE (Vesper Lynd's claim). `TryCaseEnd` appears at `loader/encode/opcodes.rs:78,270` — its encoding does not change and that file is not edited.
NO-POLLING: no new wake paths, no timers, no sleep/retry loops. The fixture watchdogs are test-side deadlines on an event-driven wait, not production polling.
NO NEW CONFIG KNOBS. Exception fidelity is not configurable; there is no 'strict exceptions' mode.

BOTH wasm32 CLOSURES STAY GREEN. `exceptions.rs`, `guards.rs`, `matching.rs`, `atom/table.rs`, and `error.rs` are SHARED interpreter code compiled for the threaded AND the cooperative closure. Both `cargo check -p beamr-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --locked` and the wasm-tests leg must be green at the final head; if any ExecError variant is added or removed, `crates/beamr-wasm/src/reasons.rs` moves in the SAME commit and its WPORT-5 coverage wall extends additively.
